messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: (R)Stan 1.0.3 release date?
parts:
We decided (informally at least) to push out
a 1.0.3 release of Stan and RStan this week.

There are a few issues I'd like to clean up
that may take a day or two (see the release notes
for 1.0.3 currently in the TO-DO.txt), but none of
them are critical enough to hold up the next release
and I'll stage them so as to be ready to go whenever.

Anyone else have anything they want to get in
for this release?

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: (R)Stan 1.0.3 release date?
parts:
On Monday, October 22, 2012 6:03:50 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Anyone else have anything they want to get in
for this release?

I'd like to try to make the manual for 1.0.3 diff-able relative to 1.0.2, but I think I am almost ready to do that.

I noticed a problem with multi_normal_cholesky and lkj_corr_cholesky_log. Originally, I didn't intend these to be exposed to the parser because they don't really make sense in the absence of a Cholesky matrix primitive type, but they got exposed so we have to deal with it. The problem is that neither checks whether the input matrix is, in fact, triangular because the C++ code implicitly assumes they are just helper functions for multi_normal and lkj_corr.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: (R)Stan 1.0.3 release date?
parts:
On Monday, October 22, 2012 6:22:27 PM UTC-4, Ben Goodrich wrote:
On Monday, October 22, 2012 6:03:50 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Anyone else have anything they want to get in
for this release?

I'd like to try to make the manual for 1.0.3 diff-able relative to 1.0.2, but I think I am almost ready to do that.

No one really expressed a strong opinion as to whether this was a good idea. So, I am going to push some changes soon unless someone speaks up.

I do something like ./diff.sh v1.0.2 HEAD and then make manual, which causes the manual to
  • Display (most) lines that have been added or changed in green text
  • Adds one "comment note" per modified page to the margin of the PDF which should be visible in Adobe products and Preview
  • Adds a "List of Corrections" page at the very end with clickable links and page references to the aforementioned "comment notes"
Limitations:
  • Not every change is processed for various reasons
  • If there is a change inside a Verbatim environment, the macros are interpreted verbatim rather than as macros and hence look messed up. See for example the second change on page 7 of the attachment. This problem can be solved by using the alltt environment rather than the Verbatim environment, which typesets things like the Verbatim environment but interprets macros. The cost of this is that we would have to escape stuff in the alltt environment, such as
parameters { # needs to be \{
  real theta; \\ comment # needs to be \\\\ comment
} # needs to be \}

We only need to make the transition from Verbatim to alltt for places where the manual changes relative to the last release, so it is not a huge deal. But I am going to wait to hear something before I start pushing changes like that.

Ben

I do have some caveats below.

I don't think it's hugely important, but that shouldn't stop
anyone from doing something they think is important, which
is why I wasn't more decisive in terms of what I thought we
should do before.

If you do want to leave it up to me or take a vote, I'd say
no -- keep things as simple as possible build-wise.

> So, I am going to push some changes soon
> unless someone speaks up.

I have a strong preference for simplicity and direct
connection between my LaTeX and the output. I've been
burned too many times by fancy pre- and post-processing
that only partly works.

So I have a very strong preference that any manual
with diffs be SEPARATE from the main manual we
distribute. If you do that, I'm happy with whatever
the actual task does and whatever the output is.

I don't want to have to put any effort into maintaining it
myself. (That's why, by the way, we still don't have a fancier
web page -- if someone wants to take over converting what we
have to use some content-generation tools AND wants to maintain
it in the future, go right ahead.)

> * Adds one "comment note" per modified page to the margin of the PDF which should be visible in Adobe products and Preview

> environment but interprets macros. The cost of this is that we would have to escape stuff in the alltt environment,
> such as

> parameters { # needs to be \{
> real theta; \\ comment # needs to be \\\\ comment
> } # needs to be \}
> |

> We only need to make the transition from Verbatim to alltt for places where the manual changes relative to the last
> release, so it is not a huge deal. But I am going to wait to hear something before I start pushing changes like that.

Will alltt handle ~ inline properly (that is, not
make it a superscript and put it in the right font)?

- Bob

P.S. This reminds me of one of my father-in-law's
favorite jokes:

Before the concert starts, a viola player complains
to the concertmaster, "A cello player turned one
of my pegs and won't tell me which one!"

He had a whole list of viola jokes he kept in his
wallet! For more of a taste:

Q: How are a violists fingers like lightning?
A: They never strike the same place twice.

He was a French horn player for the Cleveland orchestra,
and I always wondered if the violists carried French
horn jokes around, or if this was purely one way. There
are lots of viola jokes,

http://www.mit.edu/~jcb/jokes/viola.html
http://www.mit.edu/~jcb/jokes/viola2.html

and a few horn jokes:

http://www.mit.edu/~jcb/jokes/#horn

For instance, here's one he'd have liked, despite being
a Dodge man:

Q: What is the difference between a french horn section and a '57 Chevy?
A: You can tune a '57 Chevy.

No.  I want something higher contrast.  These bright
colors are very hard to read and very distracting.

They are better for highlighting the changes, though.

I just wrap changed lines in a \A{} macro and define

\newcommand{\A}{\textcolor{orange}}

in the preamble. So, we can make that whatever you want. I am not a font artist though.

I'd prefer something in the margins, which would be even
easier to scan for.

We can do that also. The reason I didn't do that originally is that things in the margin change the line spacing in the text. So, if there are a bunch of those, a word that appears on page 195 of the black-and-white PDF might be on page 196 of the diff'd PDF.

Ben
